name: work-and-bank
asks: Can a player find work and a bank, take a shift and reach an account, without typing a command?

steps.says: Start from nobody. Whether this answers ok or not_playing depends only on which journey ran before it, so the step asks for neither: it is putting the city into a known state, not asserting one.
Somebody to work and to bank.
Who is hiring. Work has no location -- an employer is external and there is nowhere to stand -- so the board is the whole of discovery, and it is why the job screen is on a key rather than a door.
The job board, opened the way F6 opens it. A screen the server can be asked to open is a screen a player can reach.
And the key itself (F6), pressed rather than the function behind it, and read back: the board has to be what comes up. A press that merely arrived is not a board a player can see.
What the board holds, which is what the screen draws.
A wage a player can read before taking the shift, not after.
And the bank, which does have a location. Every place a player can use is on the map, so a branch can be found rather than stumbled upon.
And the marks the client actually drew. The server listing a branch when asked is not a branch on anybody's map.
Pillbox Hill Branch, from config.lua. Unlike an employer a branch has an address, so there is somewhere to stand, and the server is asked whether it agrees the body is there.

The press-E prompt at the branch. A bank had a blip and deliberately no prompt for as long as there was no bank screen for the key to open. There is one now, so a branch with no prompt is a screen nobody can reach.
The city still knows who this is after all of that.
